note: Cell-line xenografts carried cetuximab to BOND but never asked the RAS question; KRAS-mutant non-response was found in patients (2006) and only then retrodicted in cells and PDX.
label: Colorectal (anti-EGFR)

engagement.note: C225 blocked EGFR in GEO colon xenografts; alone it only transiently slowed growth.
engagement.short: C225 blocks EGFR in colon xenografts
engagement.quote: Treatment of mice bearing established human GEO colon cancer xenografts with topotecan or with MAb C225 determined a transient inhibition of tumor growth because GEO tumors resumed the growth rate of untreated tumors at the end of the treatment period.
engagement.judgement: Erbitux label 12.1 names the model ('In vitro assays and in vivo animal studies have shown that cetuximab inhibits the growth...'), so model_filed is true. Antibody 225 was first dosed in A431 xenografts (Masui 1984, outside CRC); 1999 is the earliest colon xenograft found. Clin Cancer Res 1999 has no DOI; PubMed URL used.

engagement.note: Paired skin biopsies in 35 mCRC patients: cetuximab cut phospho-EGFR, phospho-MAPK and proliferation, the blockade seen in xenografts.
engagement.short: Skin pEGFR and pMAPK fell in patients
engagement.quote: In subsets of paired skin samples from 35 patients, cetuximab treatment was associated with substantial downregulation of phospho(p)-EGFR, p-MAPK and proliferation and substantial upregulation of p27(Kip1) and p-STAT3 levels.
engagement.reason: Skin pEGFR fell as xenografts said
engagement.judgement: Surrogate tissue (skin, not tumour) and abstract-level reading, hence medium. Not scored contra on Chung 2005 (doi:10.1200/JCO.2005.08.037; 4/16 EGFR-IHC-negative tumours responded) even though the label states 'No anti-tumor effects of cetuximab were observed in human tumor xenografts lacking EGFR expression': Chung attributes the discrepancy to the IHC assay, not to EGFR-independent activity. Phase I trial (Merck EMR 62202-047) not found on ClinicalTrials.gov; registry_date null.

dose.note: Mice got 0.5-1 mg IMC-C225 q3d; the clinical dose was set on saturation of clearance in patients, no model exposure target published.
dose.short: Dose set on human PK, not model
dose.quote: IMC-C225 was tested at a dose of 1 or 0.5 mg administered q3d.
dose.reason: No model exposure target to test
dose.judgement: Baselga 2000 (doi:10.1200/JCO.2000.18.4.904) chose 200-400 mg/m2 because 'antibody doses in the range of 200 to 400 mg/m(2) being associated with complete saturation of systemic clearance' in patients; Tabernero 2010 later showed weekly and every-second-week schedules equivalent on skin PD. Neither cites a xenograft exposure target, so there is nothing to compare. Clin Cancer Res 2002 has no DOI; PubMed URL used.

efficacy.note: GEO colon xenografts: C225 alone only transiently slowed growth; with topotecan, near-complete regression.
efficacy.quote: Treatment of mice bearing established human GEO colon cancer xenografts with topotecan or with MAb C225 determined a transient inhibition of tumor growth because GEO tumors resumed the growth rate of untreated tumors at the end of the treatment period.
efficacy.judgement: The pivotal lines all carry RAS-pathway mutations later shown to predict non-response in patients: GEO (KRAS G12A), DLD-1 (KRAS G13D), HT-29 (BRAF V600E). These are standard cell-line annotations (COSMIC/CCLE), not separately sourced within budget.

efficacy.note: BOND: cetuximab + irinotecan 22.9% vs 10.8% response in irinotecan-refractory mCRC, the direction the refractory DLD-1/HT-29 xenografts predicted.
efficacy.short: Combination beat monotherapy, as xenografts said
efficacy.quote: The rate of response in the combination-therapy group was significantly higher than that in the monotherapy group (22.9 percent [95 percent confidence interval, 17.5 to 29.1 percent] vs. 10.8 percent [95 percent confidence interval, 5.7 to 18.1 percent], P=0.007).
efficacy.judgement: Matching model is Prewett 2002 (PubMed 12006511): 'Combination therapy with IMC-C225 (1 mg) and the MTD of CPT-11 (150 mg/kg) resulted in a regression rate of 100 and 60% of established DLD-1 and HT-29 tumors, respectively.' Mouse regression rate and RECIST response are not the same unit, so direction only. BOND predates registration; no NCT record found in a Merck KGaA cetuximab CRC search (2000-2006).

efficacy.note: KRAS-mutant tumours did not respond (0% of responders mutant vs 68% of non-responders); the xenograft lines that regressed in mice carry KRAS/BRAF mutations.
efficacy.short: KRAS-mutant patients fail; mutant xenografts responded
efficacy.quote: A KRAS mutation was found in 13 tumors (43%) and was significantly associated with the absence of response to cetuximab (KRAS mutation in 0% of the 11 responder patients versus 68.4% of the 19 nonresponder patients; P = 0.0003).
efficacy.judgement: No model predicted KRAS non-response before patients showed it: Lievre 2006 (30 patients, retrospective) came first; Benvenuti 2007 (doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-06-4158) then retrodicted it by putting KRAS G12V into sensitive DiFi cells ('activation of the RAS signaling pathway by introduction of an activated K-RAS allele (Gly(12)Val) impairs the therapeutic effect of anti-EGFR mAbs'). Randomised confirmation: Karapetis 2008 CO.17 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa0804385; NCT00079066, first posted 2004-03-09, no results posted; KRAS-mutant OS HR 0.98) and Amado 2008 panitumumab (doi:10.1200/JCO.2007.14.7116; NCT00113763, results first posted 2014-01-03; 0% response in mutant). The contra rests on my juxtaposition of patient genotype data with the mutant genotypes of the pivotal xenograft lines; no primary source puts the two side by side. FDA restricted both labels to KRAS wild-type in 2009 (not used for the status).

efficacy.note: 85-patient PDX cohort matched clinical cetuximab response rates and retrodicted KRAS/NRAS/BRAF resistance; it then nominated HER2 amplification as a resistance driver.
efficacy.quote: xenopatients responded to the anti-EGFR antibody cetuximab with rates and extents analogous to those observed in the clinic and could be prospectively stratified as responders or nonresponders on the basis of several predictive biomarkers.
efficacy.reason: PDX retrodicts KRAS, matches response rate
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: this entry records a change of best model (PDX platform), not a reversal of the cell-line contra, which stands for that model. The comparison is retrospective concordance ('rates and extents analogous to those observed in the clinic'), abstract-level, so medium. The platform's one model-first prediction, HER2 amplification -> trastuzumab+lapatinib (HERACLES 2016), is a different drug class and is not scored here. Misale 2012 (doi:10.1038/nature11156) is the cell-line model's own forward prediction on acquired resistance: KRAS mutations selected by cetuximab in vitro were then found in 6/10 progressing patients' metastases and in plasma up to 10 months before progression (comparison stated in the paper); it does not lift the cell-line model's contra under the override rule.

safety.note: Labels report only reproductive monkey findings; acneiform rash (82%) and magnesium wasting were characterised in patients; no monkey-patient comparison found.
safety.quote: Acneiform rash occurred in 82% of the 1373 patients who received ERBITUX across clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Hypomagnesemia was first described in patients: Schrag 2005 (doi:10.1093/jnci/dji242), 'We report that patients treated with cetuximab, a monoclonal antibody against the epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR), occasionally develop a magnesium wasting syndrome with inappropriate urinary excretion.' Erbitux label 5.6 gives 55%, Vectibix label (setid e0fa4bca-f245-4d92-ae29-b0c630a315c2) 38%, dermatologic toxicity 90%. Whether monkey toxicology showed skin or magnesium findings could not be verified: the Vectibix 2006 FDA pharmacology review (accessdata nda/2006/125147s0000_PharmR.pdf) is a scanned image with no text layer and OCR was unavailable; the 2004 Erbitux review index returned 404. Section 13 of both labels lists only menstrual-cycle findings in cynomolgus monkeys (the label sentence is truncated by the fetch tool, so the patient-side sentence is quoted). Not scored contra on monkey silence because silence was not verified. Year 2004 is the Erbitux approval; monkey studies predate it.
